items.name: Vrat Cumin Sabudana Khichdi

ingredients.name: Potatoes, boiled and cut into cubes

steps: Rinse the tapioca pearls in three changes of cool water, drain, and add 240 ml fresh water; soak for 4–6 hours, then tip them into a sieve for 5 minutes so the grains separate cleanly.
Drain the soaked pearls thoroughly and rub the coarse peanut meal through them so they separate. Let it drain for 2 minutes without pressing harder than the recipe's texture requires.

Toast cumin in ghee, brown the potato cubes, and fold in the coated pearls over moderate heat. Give the spices about 30 seconds before adding the larger pieces, then continue over medium-low heat for 4–5 minutes, moving the pan often, until the raw aroma is gone.

Cover only until the centers turn translucent, then uncover, season, and add the lemon juice away from the flame. Maintain gentle medium heat for 8–10 minutes, stirring every 3 minutes, until every pearl is translucent with no opaque pin at its center.
Rest Vrat Cumin Sabudana Khichdi 7 minutes covered off the burner; check the final consistency and serve it warm without prolonged holding.
items.guidance: Careful soaking keeps this fasting khichdi separate rather than gummy Vata: serve it warm and add a little ghee if the meal feels dry. Pitta: keep the sharp spices modest and favor coriander or fennel. Kapha: use fewer peanuts and potatoes and choose a small portion.
provenance: original lacto-vegetarian recipe developed for the R3 regional and practical cooking collection

items.name: Vrat Baked Sabudana Vada
steps: Rinse the tapioca pearls in three changes of cool water, drain, and add 220 ml fresh water; soak for 4–6 hours, then tip them into a sieve for 5 minutes so the grains separate cleanly.

Mix the drained pearls with the mashed potato, coarse peanuts, crushed cumin, chopped cilantro, and salt. Mix for 1 minute with the heat off, stopping when the seasonings are even and a pressed spoonful holds together without crumbling.

Shape compact patties with damp hands, arrange them on a warmed tray, and brush their surfaces lightly with melted ghee. Aim for an even 12–15 mm thickness; repair cracks before the piece reaches the hot surface.

Bake until the bases are firm, turn each patty once, and continue until both faces are evenly golden. Keep the oven at 200°C (400°F) for 20–24 minutes, checking until the surface looks dry, brown freckles appear, and the center springs back.
Set Vrat Baked Sabudana Vada on a rack or heatproof board for 4 minutes so steam escapes without softening the browned surfaces; serve while the center is still warm.
items.guidance: Baking gives fasting sabudana patties a crisp surface with less fat Vata: serve it warm and add a little ghee if the meal feels dry. Pitta: keep the sharp spices modest and favor coriander or fennel. Kapha: eat one small patty and increase cumin while reducing peanut.
provenance: original lacto-vegetarian recipe developed for the R3 regional and practical cooking collection

items.name: Vrat Sabudana Potato Thalipeeth
steps: Rinse the tapioca pearls in three changes of cool water, drain, and add 200 ml fresh water; soak for 4–6 hours, then tip them into a sieve for 5 minutes so the grains separate cleanly.
Knead the drained pearls, grated potato, fine peanut meal, cumin, and salt into a soft fasting dough. Knead for 6 minutes, stopping when the dough feels cohesive and a thumb press closes slowly.

Press one portion between damp palms, transfer it to a warm greased griddle, and thin it gently with wet fingertips. Aim for an even 3–4 mm thickness; repair cracks before the piece reaches the hot surface.

Cook until the lower face releases, turn with a wide spatula, and brown the second side with only a trace more ghee. Hold the griddle at medium heat and allow 2–3 minutes on the first face and 1–2 minutes after turning, until the surface looks dry, brown freckles appear, and the center springs back.
Stack Vrat Sabudana Potato Thalipeeth beneath a clean cloth for 3 minutes; serve it warm once the center has relaxed but the browned faces are still dry.
items.guidance: A thin shape makes this sabudana thalipeeth crisper and easier to digest Vata: serve it warm and add a little ghee if the meal feels dry. Pitta: keep the sharp spices modest and favor coriander or fennel. Kapha: keep the cake thin, use little ghee, and eat a modest serving.
provenance: original lacto-vegetarian recipe developed for the R3 regional and practical cooking collection

items.name: Vrat Cardamom Sabudana Kheer
steps: Rinse the tapioca pearls in three changes of cool water, drain, and add 110 ml fresh water; soak for 4–6 hours, then tip them into a sieve for 5 minutes so the grains separate cleanly.

Simmer the soaked pearls in part of the warmed milk until their centers become clear. Maintain steady low heat for 6–8 minutes, stirring every 3 minutes, until every pearl is translucent with no opaque pin at its center.

Pour in the remaining milk gradually and stir often as the kheer thickens around the translucent pearls. Keep the pan over moderate heat for 2–3 minutes after the final addition, folding from the bottom so the main pieces remain intact.

Remove the pot from direct heat, dissolve the crushed rock sugar, and finish with cardamom and sliced pistachios. Leave the pan off the flame for 5 minutes, then taste and correct the final balance before serving at the stated temperature.
Rest Vrat Cardamom Sabudana Kheer 7 minutes covered off the burner; check the final consistency and serve it warm without prolonged holding.
items.guidance: This festival kheer is cooling and rich, so a small warm portion is sufficient Vata: serve it warm and add a little ghee if the meal feels dry. Pitta: keep the sharp spices modest and favor coriander or fennel. Kapha: take only a few spoonfuls and reduce both sweetener and nuts.
provenance: original lacto-vegetarian recipe developed for the R3 regional and practical cooking collection

items.name: Vrat Pumpkin Sabudana Pot

ingredients.name: Pumpkin, peeled and cut into tiny cubes

steps: Measure 240 ml (about 1 cup) water for Vrat Pumpkin Sabudana Pot; bring it to a full boil, then keep it covered and hot for the additions below.
Rinse the tapioca pearls in three changes of cool water, drain, and add 190 ml fresh water; soak for 4–6 hours, then tip them into a sieve for 5 minutes so the grains separate cleanly.

Soften cumin and grated ginger in ghee, then add the tiny pumpkin cubes and turn them until glossy. Keep the pan over gentle medium heat for 1–2 minutes after the final addition, folding from the bottom so the main pieces remain intact.

Splash in hot water, cover until the pumpkin is nearly tender, and spread the drained pearls across the surface. Maintain low heat for 13–15 minutes, stirring every 4 minutes, until every pearl is translucent with no opaque pin at its center.

Cook gently until the pearls clear, folding only twice so the pumpkin remains visible, then season. Maintain steady low heat for 6–8 minutes, stirring every 5 minutes, until every pearl is translucent with no opaque pin at its center.
Rest Vrat Pumpkin Sabudana Pot 4 minutes covered off the burner; check the final consistency and serve it warm without prolonged holding.
items.guidance: Pumpkin adds moisture to this fasting sabudana main Vata: serve it warm and add a little ghee if the meal feels dry. Pitta: keep the sharp spices modest and favor coriander or fennel. Kapha: reduce the pearl portion and add more ginger.
provenance: original lacto-vegetarian recipe developed for the R3 regional and practical cooking collection

items.name: Vrat Sweet Potato Sabudana Pilaf

ingredients.name: Sweet potato, peeled and cut into small cubes

steps: For Vrat Sweet Potato Sabudana Pilaf, rinse the tapioca pearls in three changes of cool water, drain, and add 190 ml fresh water; soak for 4–6 hours, then tip them into a sieve for 5 minutes so the grains separate cleanly.

Brown the sweet-potato cubes slowly in ghee with crushed fennel until their edges caramelize. Give the spices about 30 seconds before adding the larger pieces, then continue over gentle medium heat for 3–4 minutes, moving the pan often, until the raw aroma is gone.

Add the drained pearls and chopped peanuts, cover briefly, and shake the pan as the centers turn translucent. Maintain low heat for 6–8 minutes, stirring every 5 minutes, until every pearl is translucent with no opaque pin at its center.

Uncover to release steam, season the pilaf, and sprinkle in the lemon juice once it leaves the heat. Leave the pan off the flame for 6 minutes, then taste and correct the final balance before serving at the stated temperature.
Rest Vrat Sweet Potato Sabudana Pilaf 4 minutes covered off the burner; check the final consistency and serve it warm without prolonged holding.
items.guidance: Fennel balances the sweetness of this root-and-sabudana fasting pilaf Vata: serve it warm and add a little ghee if the meal feels dry. Pitta: keep the sharp spices modest and favor coriander or fennel. Kapha: use a smaller portion and sharpen the seasoning with ginger or black pepper.
provenance: original lacto-vegetarian recipe developed for the R3 regional and practical cooking collection

items.name: Vrat Chayote Sabudana Upma

ingredients.name: Fresh ginger, cut into fine slivers

steps: For Vrat Chayote Sabudana Upma, rinse the tapioca pearls in three changes of cool water, drain, and add 190 ml fresh water; soak for 4–6 hours, then tip them into a sieve for 5 minutes so the grains separate cleanly.

Toast cumin and ginger slivers in ghee, then sauté the chayote dice until their edges turn translucent. Give the spices about 30 seconds before adding the larger pieces, then continue over steady low heat for 3–4 minutes, moving the pan often, until the raw aroma is gone.

Spread the drained pearls over the vegetable, cover for a few minutes, and lift them gently from below rather than stirring hard. Maintain moderate heat for 6–8 minutes, stirring every 5 minutes, until every pearl is translucent with no opaque pin at its center.

Stop cooking when the pearls are clear, season the upma, and scatter chopped cilantro over the loose mixture. Leave the pan off the flame for 6 minutes, then taste and correct the final balance before serving at the stated temperature.
Rest Vrat Chayote Sabudana Upma 6 minutes covered off the burner; check the final consistency and serve it warm without prolonged holding.
items.guidance: Juicy chayote keeps this fasting upma lighter than a potato version Vata: serve it warm and add a little ghee if the meal feels dry. Pitta: keep the sharp spices modest and favor coriander or fennel. Kapha: use a smaller portion and sharpen the seasoning with ginger or black pepper.
provenance: original lacto-vegetarian recipe developed for the R3 regional and practical cooking collection

items.name: Vrat Lotus Seed Sabudana Khichdi

ingredients.name: Potatoes, boiled and cut into cubes

steps: Rinse the tapioca pearls in three changes of cool water, drain, and add 180 ml fresh water; soak for 4–6 hours, then tip them into a sieve for 5 minutes so the grains separate cleanly.

Dry-roast the lotus seeds until crisp and break the larger ones into halves after they cool. Give the spices about 30 seconds before adding the larger pieces, then continue over steady low heat for 2–3 minutes, moving the pan often, until the raw aroma is gone.

Bloom cumin and pepper in ghee, brown the potato cubes, and fold in the drained tapioca pearls. Give the spices about 30 seconds before adding the larger pieces, then continue over moderate heat for 3–4 minutes, moving the pan often, until the raw aroma is gone.

Add the roasted seed halves when the pearls become translucent, toss gently, and season before serving warm. Give the spices about 30 seconds before adding the larger pieces, then continue over medium-low heat for 4–5 minutes, moving the pan often, until the raw aroma is gone.
Rest Vrat Lotus Seed Sabudana Khichdi 7 minutes covered off the burner; check the final consistency and serve it warm without prolonged holding.
items.guidance: Crisp lotus seeds contrast with soft pearls in this festival khichdi Vata: serve it warm and add a little ghee if the meal feels dry. Pitta: keep the sharp spices modest and favor coriander or fennel. Kapha: reduce both potato and ghee and keep the bowl small.
provenance: original lacto-vegetarian recipe developed for the R3 regional and practical cooking collection

items.name: Vrat Coconut Lemon Sabudana
steps: Rinse the tapioca pearls in three changes of cool water, drain, and add 210 ml fresh water; soak for 4–6 hours, then tip them into a sieve for 5 minutes so the grains separate cleanly.

Warm cumin in coconut oil and add the drained pearls in an even layer. Give the spices about 30 seconds before adding the larger pieces, then continue over gentle medium heat for 2–3 minutes, moving the pan often, until the raw aroma is gone.

Cover briefly, then lift the pearls from the edges until they turn translucent without clumping. Maintain low heat for 6–8 minutes, stirring every 3 minutes, until every pearl is translucent with no opaque pin at its center.

Fold through the grated coconut and salt, remove the pan from heat, and finish with lemon juice and cilantro. Leave the pan off the flame for 4 minutes, then taste and correct the final balance before serving at the stated temperature.
Rest Vrat Coconut Lemon Sabudana 4 minutes covered off the burner; check the final consistency and serve it warm without prolonged holding.
items.guidance: Coconut and lemon give sabudana a bright festival finish Vata: serve it warm and add a little ghee if the meal feels dry. Pitta: use less lemon and eat the dish only warm, not hot. Kapha: keep coconut and oil light.
provenance: original lacto-vegetarian recipe developed for the R3 regional and practical cooking collection

items.name: Vrat Soft Savory Sabudana Porridge
steps: Measure 350 ml (about 1 1/2 cups) water and 500 ml almond drink for Vrat Soft Savory Sabudana Porridge; heat them separately over low heat so neither addition dilutes or cools the next stage unexpectedly.
Rinse the tapioca pearls in three changes of cool water, drain, and add 160 ml fresh water; soak for 4–6 hours, then tip them into a sieve for 5 minutes so the grains separate cleanly.

Simmer the soaked pearls in hot water until they begin to lose their opaque centers. Maintain steady low heat for 13–15 minutes, stirring every 4 minutes, until every pearl is translucent with no opaque pin at its center.

Add the warmed almond drink, ground cumin, and grated ginger, then stir gently as the porridge becomes silky. Keep the pan over moderate heat for 1–2 minutes after the final addition, folding from the bottom so the main pieces remain intact.

Season the soft mixture, draw it off the heat, and melt a little ghee across the surface before serving. Leave the pan off the flame for 6 minutes, then taste and correct the final balance before serving at the stated temperature.
Rest Vrat Soft Savory Sabudana Porridge 6 minutes covered off the burner; check the final consistency and serve it warm without prolonged holding.
items.guidance: Extra liquid turns sabudana into a soft fasting breakfast rather than a dry pilaf Vata: serve it warm and add a little ghee if the meal feels dry. Pitta: keep the sharp spices modest and favor coriander or fennel. Kapha: use a smaller portion and sharpen the seasoning with ginger or black pepper.
provenance: original lacto-vegetarian recipe developed for the R3 regional and practical cooking collection

items.name: Vrat Amaranth Pumpkin Khichdi

ingredients.name: Amaranth grain, rinsed in a fine sieve
Pumpkin, peeled and cut into small cubes

steps: Bring 950 ml (about 4 cups) water to a boil in a separate kettle and hold it hot, covered, so Vrat Amaranth Pumpkin Khichdi never loses its simmer.

Warm cumin and grated ginger in ghee, then stir the tiny amaranth grains through the fragrant pot. Give the spices about 30 seconds before adding the larger pieces, then continue over low heat for 4–5 minutes, moving the pan often, until the raw aroma is gone.

Add the pumpkin cubes and hot water, bring to a boil, and lower the heat under a partly covered lid. Maintain steady low heat for 13–15 minutes, stirring every 3 minutes, until a thin knife slides through the largest piece without resistance.

Cook until the grains swell into a soft mass and the pumpkin yields, then season and rest the khichdi. Maintain moderate heat for 15–17 minutes, stirring every 3 minutes, until a thin knife slides through the largest piece without resistance.
Fluff or stir Vrat Amaranth Pumpkin Khichdi once after its off-heat rest, check the final consistency, and serve it warm without prolonged holding.
items.guidance: Pumpkin softens the earthy character of amaranth in this fasting khichdi Vata: serve it warm and add a little ghee if the meal feels dry. Pitta: keep the sharp spices modest and favor coriander or fennel. Kapha: use a smaller portion and sharpen the seasoning with ginger or black pepper.
provenance: original lacto-vegetarian recipe developed for the R3 regional and practical cooking collection

items.name: Vrat Amaranth Fennel Porridge

ingredients.name: Amaranth grain, rinsed in a fine sieve

steps: Measure 450 ml (about 2 cups) water and 520 ml oat drink for Vrat Amaranth Fennel Porridge; heat them separately over low heat so neither addition dilutes or cools the next stage unexpectedly.

Simmer the rinsed amaranth in hot water until the grains swell and the liquid looks glossy. Maintain steady low heat for 14–16 minutes, stirring every 5 minutes, until a grain pressed between two fingers has no chalky center.

Pour in the warmed oat drink, add ground fennel, and continue stirring until the porridge is creamy. Keep the pan over moderate heat for 2–3 minutes after the final addition, folding from the bottom so the main pieces remain intact.

Take the pot off the flame before dissolving the crushed rock sugar and scattering in the cardamom. Leave the pan off the flame for 3 minutes, then taste and correct the final balance before serving at the stated temperature.
Rest Vrat Amaranth Fennel Porridge 7 minutes covered off the burner; check the final consistency and serve it warm without prolonged holding.
items.guidance: Fennel makes this amaranth fasting porridge gently aromatic Vata: serve it warm and add a little ghee if the meal feels dry. Pitta: keep the sharp spices modest and favor coriander or fennel. Kapha: use a smaller portion and sharpen the seasoning with ginger or black pepper.
provenance: original lacto-vegetarian recipe developed for the R3 regional and practical cooking collection

items.name: Vrat Amaranth Potato Flatbread
steps: Prepare 90 ml (about 1/2 cup) hot water before starting Vrat Amaranth Potato Flatbread; keep one small ladle in reserve in case the base tightens early.

Combine the amaranth flour with mashed potato, crushed cumin, cilantro, and salt, adding hot water only as needed. Mix for 1 minute with the heat off, stopping when the seasonings are even and a pressed spoonful holds together without crumbling.
Pat a dough portion into a thin round between oiled sheets and peel away the upper sheet carefully. Knead for 6 minutes, stopping when the dough feels cohesive and a thumb press closes slowly.

Transfer the round to a warm griddle, cook until firm, and brown both faces with a light brushing of ghee. Hold the griddle at medium heat and allow 2–3 minutes on the first face and 1–2 minutes after turning, until the surface looks dry, brown freckles appear, and the center springs back.
Stack Vrat Amaranth Potato Flatbread beneath a clean cloth for 6 minutes; serve it warm once the center has relaxed but the browned faces are still dry.
items.guidance: Mashed potato makes gluten-free amaranth dough pliable enough for a fasting flatbread Vata: serve it warm and add a little ghee if the meal feels dry. Pitta: keep the sharp spices modest and favor coriander or fennel. Kapha: make the breads thin and limit both potato and ghee.
provenance: original lacto-vegetarian recipe developed for the R3 regional and practical cooking collection

items.name: Vrat Amaranth Pumpkin Pancake
steps: Lay out the prepared amaranth grain, pumpkin, and fennel seeds in their order of use; drain wet components for 2 minutes before they reach hot fat.

Whisk the amaranth flour with mashed pumpkin, ground fennel, salt, and enough warm almond drink for a thick batter. Give the spices about 30 seconds before adding the larger pieces, then continue over medium-low heat for 3–4 minutes, moving the pan often, until the raw aroma is gone.
Rest the mixture briefly, then spoon small rounds onto a greased griddle and spread them without pressing. Aim for an even 2–3 mm thickness; repair cracks before the piece reaches the hot surface.

Wait until the edges dry before turning each pancake, and cook the second face until the center feels set. Hold the griddle at medium heat and allow 2–3 minutes on the first face and 1–2 minutes after turning, until the surface looks dry, brown freckles appear, and the center springs back.
Stack Vrat Amaranth Pumpkin Pancake beneath a clean cloth for 4 minutes; serve it warm once the center has relaxed but the browned faces are still dry.
items.guidance: Pumpkin keeps these fasting amaranth pancakes tender without eggs Vata: serve it warm and add a little ghee if the meal feels dry. Pitta: keep the sharp spices modest and favor coriander or fennel. Kapha: use a smaller portion and sharpen the seasoning with ginger or black pepper.
provenance: original lacto-vegetarian recipe developed for the R3 regional and practical cooking collection

items.name: Vrat Amaranth Sesame Laddoo

ingredients.name: Sesame seeds, toasted and ground coarse

steps: Set the amaranth grain, sesame seeds, and jaggery in separate bowls and complete the listed rinsing, cutting, or grinding before heating the pan.

Toast the popped amaranth and coarse sesame together until the mixture smells nutty. Give the spices about 30 seconds before adding the larger pieces, then continue over steady low heat for 2–3 minutes, moving the pan often, until the raw aroma is gone.

Melt the grated jaggery with a spoonful of water, cook it to a sticky syrup, and stir in the warm ghee. Give the spices about 30 seconds before adding the larger pieces, then continue over moderate heat for 2–3 minutes, moving the pan often, until the raw aroma is gone.

Work the hot syrup and cardamom through the grains, then shape small balls with lightly greased palms before the mixture cools. Aim for an even 3–4 mm thickness; repair cracks before the piece reaches the hot surface.
Rest Vrat Amaranth Sesame Laddoo 3 minutes covered off the burner; check the final consistency and serve it warm without prolonged holding.
items.guidance: These dense festival sweets combine popped amaranth with sesame and jaggery Vata: serve it warm and add a little ghee if the meal feels dry. Pitta: keep the sharp spices modest and favor coriander or fennel. Kapha: eat only one small ball and reduce the sweetener.
provenance: original lacto-vegetarian recipe developed for the R3 regional and practical cooking collection

items.name: Vrat Amaranth Cardamom Kheer

ingredients.name: Amaranth grain, rinsed in a fine sieve

steps: Lay out the prepared amaranth grain, green cardamom, and almonds in their order of use; drain wet components for 2 minutes before they reach hot fat.

Cook the rinsed amaranth in a portion of the warmed milk until the grains bloom and soften. Give the spices about 30 seconds before adding the larger pieces, then continue over steady low heat for 3–4 minutes, moving the pan often, until the raw aroma is gone.

Add the remaining milk in stages, stirring the base so it thickens without catching on the pot. Keep the pan over moderate heat for 1–2 minutes after the final addition, folding from the bottom so the main pieces remain intact.

Remove the kheer from direct heat, dissolve the crushed rock sugar, and finish with cardamom and sliced almonds. Leave the pan off the flame for 6 minutes, then taste and correct the final balance before serving at the stated temperature.
Rest Vrat Amaranth Cardamom Kheer 6 minutes covered off the burner; check the final consistency and serve it warm without prolonged holding.
items.guidance: Amaranth gives this fasting milk pudding a fine, bead-like texture Vata: serve it warm and add a little ghee if the meal feels dry. Pitta: keep the sharp spices modest and favor coriander or fennel. Kapha: choose a small warm portion with less sweetener and fewer almonds.
provenance: original lacto-vegetarian recipe developed for the R3 regional and practical cooking collection

items.name: Vrat Amaranth Chayote Pot

ingredients.name: Amaranth grain, rinsed in a fine sieve
Fresh ginger, cut into fine slivers

steps: Prepare 900 ml (about 3 3/4 cups) hot water before starting Vrat Amaranth Chayote Pot; keep one small ladle in reserve in case the base tightens early.

Bloom cumin and ginger slivers in ghee, then add the chayote dice and turn them until glossy. Give the spices about 30 seconds before adding the larger pieces, then continue over gentle medium heat for 4–5 minutes, moving the pan often, until the raw aroma is gone.

Stir in the rinsed amaranth and hot water, bring the pot to a boil, and lower the heat. Maintain low heat for 12–14 minutes, stirring every 3 minutes, until a thin knife slides through the largest piece without resistance.

Cook partly covered until the grains thicken around the tender vegetable, then season and rest before serving. Maintain steady low heat for 7–9 minutes, stirring every 3 minutes, until a thin knife slides through the largest piece without resistance.
Fluff or stir Vrat Amaranth Chayote Pot once after its off-heat rest, check the final consistency, and serve it warm without prolonged holding.
items.guidance: Chayote adds welcome moisture to a simple amaranth fasting meal Vata: serve it warm and add a little ghee if the meal feels dry. Pitta: keep the sharp spices modest and favor coriander or fennel. Kapha: use a smaller portion and sharpen the seasoning with ginger or black pepper.
provenance: original lacto-vegetarian recipe developed for the R3 regional and practical cooking collection

items.name: Vrat Amaranth Potato Pilaf

ingredients.name: Amaranth grain, rinsed in a fine sieve
Potatoes, peeled and cut into small cubes

steps: Bring 780 ml (about 3 1/4 cups) water to a boil in a separate kettle and hold it hot, covered, so Vrat Amaranth Potato Pilaf never loses its simmer.

Brown the potato cubes in ghee with cumin until their edges develop a light crust. Give the spices about 30 seconds before adding the larger pieces, then continue over gentle medium heat for 3–4 minutes, moving the pan often, until the raw aroma is gone.

Add the amaranth, cracked pepper, and hot water, then cover as soon as the pot returns to a boil. Maintain low heat for 14–16 minutes, stirring every 5 minutes, until a thin knife slides through the largest piece without resistance.

Cook until the grains are tender and the liquid is absorbed, loosen the pilaf gently, and season. Maintain steady low heat for 13–15 minutes, stirring every 3 minutes, until a thin knife slides through the largest piece without resistance.
Rest Vrat Amaranth Potato Pilaf 6 minutes covered off the burner; check the final consistency and serve it warm without prolonged holding.
items.guidance: Potato makes this amaranth pilaf particularly grounding Vata: serve it warm and add a little ghee if the meal feels dry. Pitta: keep the sharp spices modest and favor coriander or fennel. Kapha: reduce the potato and ghee and increase black pepper.
provenance: original lacto-vegetarian recipe developed for the R3 regional and practical cooking collection

items.name: Vrat Amaranth Sesame Brittle
steps: Complete the chopping and grinding for the amaranth grain, sesame seeds, and jaggery, then set each component beside the stove in the order it enters the recipe.

Combine the popped amaranth, toasted sesame, and ground cardamom in a warm bowl. Give the spices about 30 seconds before adding the larger pieces, then continue over low heat for 4–5 minutes, moving the pan often, until the raw aroma is gone.

Melt the grated jaggery with a spoonful of water and cook until a drop firms quickly in cool water. Maintain steady low heat for 15–17 minutes, stirring every 3 minutes, until a grain pressed between two fingers has no chalky center.

Stir in the grain mixture, spread it thinly on a greased tray, and score small pieces before the brittle hardens. Keep the pan over moderate heat for 1–2 minutes after the final addition, folding from the bottom so the main pieces remain intact.
Rest Vrat Amaranth Sesame Brittle 5 minutes covered off the burner; check the final consistency and serve it warm without prolonged holding.
items.guidance: A thin sheet keeps this concentrated festival brittle appropriately portioned Vata: serve it warm and add a little ghee if the meal feels dry. Pitta: keep the sharp spices modest and favor coriander or fennel. Kapha: limit the serving to one small piece.
provenance: original lacto-vegetarian recipe developed for the R3 regional and practical cooking collection

items.name: Vrat Apple Amaranth Bake

ingredients.name: Apples, peeled and cut into wedges

steps: Set the apples, amaranth grain, and almonds in separate bowls and complete the listed rinsing, cutting, or grinding before heating the pan.
Arrange the apple wedges in a greased baking dish and dust them evenly with ground cinnamon. Keep the layer loose and even, with no pooled liquid, so every portion receives the same balance.

Mix the popped amaranth with chopped almonds and melted ghee, then scatter the rough topping over the fruit. Mix for 1 minute with the heat off, stopping when the seasonings are even and a pressed spoonful holds together without crumbling.

Drizzle lightly with maple syrup and bake until the apples soften and the topping becomes crisp at the edges. Keep the oven at 190°C (375°F) for 20–24 minutes, checking until the fruit yields to a thin knife and the exposed edges are lightly browned.
Set Vrat Apple Amaranth Bake on a rack or heatproof board for 5 minutes so steam escapes without softening the browned surfaces; serve while the center is still warm.
items.guidance: Baking makes fruit appropriate for a warm festival dessert without combining it with milk Vata: serve it warm and add a little ghee if the meal feels dry. Pitta: keep the sharp spices modest and favor coriander or fennel. Kapha: use a smaller portion and sharpen the seasoning with ginger or black pepper.

items.name: Vrat Buckwheat Cumin Khichdi

ingredients.name: Potatoes, peeled and cut into small cubes

steps: For Vrat Buckwheat Cumin Khichdi, heat 760 ml (about 3 1/4 cups) water until vigorously boiling, then lower it to a bare simmer beside the main pot for measured additions.

Warm cumin and grated ginger in ghee, then brown the potato cubes lightly in the aromatic pot. Give the spices about 30 seconds before adding the larger pieces, then continue over steady low heat for 2–3 minutes, moving the pan often, until the raw aroma is gone.

Stir in the buckwheat groats and hot water, cover, and cook gently until the grains split and soften. Maintain moderate heat for 15–17 minutes, stirring every 4 minutes, until a thin knife slides through the largest piece without resistance.

Rest the khichdi off the heat, fluff it without crushing the potato, and season before serving. Leave the pan off the flame for 5 minutes, then taste and correct the final balance before serving at the stated temperature.
Fluff or stir Vrat Buckwheat Cumin Khichdi once after its off-heat rest, check the final consistency, and serve it warm without prolonged holding.
items.guidance: Buckwheat makes this fasting khichdi warming and comparatively light Vata: serve it warm and add a little ghee if the meal feels dry. Pitta: keep the sharp spices modest and favor coriander or fennel. Kapha: use a smaller portion and sharpen the seasoning with ginger or black pepper.
provenance: original lacto-vegetarian recipe developed for the R3 regional and practical cooking collection

items.name: Vrat Buckwheat Potato Roti
steps: Measure 90 ml (about 1/2 cup) water for Vrat Buckwheat Potato Roti; bring it to a full boil, then keep it covered and hot for the additions below.

Mix the buckwheat flour with mashed potato, crushed cumin, and salt, adding warm water until the dough holds. Knead for 7 minutes, stopping when the dough feels cohesive and a thumb press closes slowly.
Pat a small portion between greased sheets into an even round and peel back the upper sheet. Aim for an even 2–3 mm thickness; repair cracks before the piece reaches the hot surface.

Lay the roti on a hot griddle, wait until it firms before turning, and brown both sides with a trace of ghee. Hold the griddle at medium heat and allow 2–3 minutes on the first face and 1–2 minutes after turning, until the surface looks dry, brown freckles appear, and the center springs back.
Stack Vrat Buckwheat Potato Roti beneath a clean cloth for 6 minutes; serve it warm once the center has relaxed but the browned faces are still dry.

items.name: Vrat Buckwheat Fennel Dosa
steps: Heat 360 ml (about 1 1/2 cups) water until vigorously boiling, then lower it to a bare simmer beside the main pot for measured additions.
Whisk the buckwheat flour with yogurt, ground fennel, ginger, salt, and enough water for a flowing batter. Whisk for 60 seconds, scraping the bottom and corners until no dry pockets or lumps remain.

Rest the batter briefly, then pour a thin spiral onto a hot griddle and fill the gaps with the back of the ladle. Hold the griddle at medium heat and allow 2–3 minutes on the first face and 1–2 minutes after turning, until the surface looks dry, brown freckles appear, and the center springs back.

Drizzle a little ghee around the edge, turn when the surface dries, and cook the second side only until set. Hold the griddle at medium heat and allow 2–3 minutes on the first face and 1–2 minutes after turning, until the surface looks dry, brown freckles appear, and the center springs back.
Stack Vrat Buckwheat Fennel Dosa beneath a clean cloth for 6 minutes; serve it warm once the center has relaxed but the browned faces are still dry.

items.name: Vrat Buckwheat Pumpkin Chilla
steps: Set aside 260 ml (about 1 cup) freshly boiled water for Vrat Buckwheat Pumpkin Chilla, reserving about 60 ml to correct the final consistency.

Whisk the buckwheat flour with mashed pumpkin, crushed cumin, cilantro, salt, and enough water for a thick batter. Whisk for 40 seconds, scraping the bottom and corners until no dry pockets or lumps remain.

Spoon a modest round onto a greased griddle and spread it gently so the pumpkin remains evenly distributed. Hold the griddle at medium heat and allow 2–3 minutes on the first face and 1–2 minutes after turning, until the surface looks dry, brown freckles appear, and the center springs back.

Turn after the lower face releases cleanly, then cook the second side until the center no longer feels damp. Hold the griddle at medium heat and allow 2–3 minutes on the first face and 1–2 minutes after turning, until the surface looks dry, brown freckles appear, and the center springs back.

items.name: Vrat Buckwheat Dumpling Kadhi
steps: Prepare 820 ml (about 3 1/2 cups) hot water before starting Vrat Buckwheat Dumpling Kadhi; keep one small ladle in reserve in case the base tightens early.
Knead buckwheat flour and mashed potato with salt, then roll the soft dough into small fasting dumplings. Knead for 7 minutes, stopping when the dough feels cohesive and a thumb press closes slowly.

Poach the dumplings until they rise and firm, lift them out, and whisk the yogurt into the warm cooking liquid. Give the spices about 30 seconds before adding the larger pieces, then continue over medium-low heat for 4–5 minutes, moving the pan often, until the raw aroma is gone.

Simmer the kadhi gently with cumin bloomed in ghee, return the dumplings, and warm them until they absorb the tangy broth. Maintain gentle medium heat for 14–16 minutes, stirring every 3 minutes, until a thin knife slides through the largest piece without resistance.
Rest Vrat Buckwheat Dumpling Kadhi 6 minutes covered off the burner; check the final consistency and serve it warm without prolonged holding.

items.name: Vrat Buckwheat Sweet Potato Cakes
steps: Set the buckwheat groats, sweet potato, and fennel seeds in separate bowls and complete the listed rinsing, cutting, or grinding before heating the pan.

Fresh ginger, cut into fine slivers

Toast cumin and ginger slivers in ghee, then stir the buckwheat groats until they smell nutty. Give the spices about 30 seconds before adding the larger pieces, then continue over medium-low heat for 2–3 minutes, moving the pan often, until the raw aroma is gone.

Pour in hot water and simmer until the grains begin to soften before adding the pumpkin chunks. Maintain gentle medium heat for 13–15 minutes, stirring every 3 minutes, until a thin knife slides through the largest piece without resistance.

steps: Measure 420 ml (about 1 3/4 cups) water and 520 ml almond drink for Vrat Buckwheat Almond Porridge; heat them separately over low heat so neither addition dilutes or cools the next stage unexpectedly.

Simmer the buckwheat groats in hot water until they split and become tender. Maintain medium-low heat for 13–15 minutes, stirring every 3 minutes, until a grain pressed between two fingers has no chalky center.

Add the warmed almond drink and continue cooking until the mixture reaches a loose porridge consistency. Keep the pan over gentle medium heat for 1–2 minutes after the final addition, folding from the bottom so the main pieces remain intact.

Remove the pot from heat, stir in the crushed rock sugar and cardamom, and garnish with sliced almonds. Leave the pan off the flame for 4 minutes, then taste and correct the final balance before serving at the stated temperature.

Roast the buckwheat flour in ghee over low heat until its color deepens and the aroma turns nutty. Give the spices about 30 seconds before adding the larger pieces, then continue over low heat for 4–5 minutes, moving the pan often, until the raw aroma is gone.

Pour in hot water gradually while stirring firmly, and cook until the paste leaves the sides of the pan. Maintain steady low heat for 14–16 minutes, stirring every 3 minutes, until a grain pressed between two fingers has no chalky center.

Simmer the pumpkin chunks with ginger slivers until they are tender but still hold their corners. Maintain steady low heat for 14–16 minutes, stirring every 3 minutes, until a thin knife slides through the largest piece without resistance.
Grind the coconut with cumin and hot broth, then fold the smooth paste through the pot. Work in 4 short pulses, pausing between them so the mixture stays cool and retains the intended texture.

Season the stew, remove it from direct heat, and finish the surface with a restrained drizzle of coconut oil. Maintain medium-low heat for 13–15 minutes, stirring every 5 minutes, until a thin knife slides through the largest piece without resistance.
Fluff or stir Vrat Pumpkin Coconut Stew once after its off-heat rest, check the final consistency, and serve it warm without prolonged holding.
items.guidance: A mild coconut broth makes pumpkin suitable for a quiet fasting main Vata: serve it warm and add a little ghee if the meal feels dry. Pitta: keep the sharp spices modest and favor coriander or fennel. Kapha: use a smaller portion and sharpen the seasoning with ginger or black pepper.

items.name: Vrat Baked Yam Patties
steps: Complete the chopping and grinding for the yam, chestnuts, and cumin seeds, then set each component beside the stove in the order it enters the recipe.

Mix the mashed yam with chestnut meal, crushed cumin, chopped cilantro, and salt. Mix for 1 minute with the heat off, stopping when the seasonings are even and a pressed spoonful holds together without crumbling.
Shape broad thin patties, arrange them on a warmed tray, and brush the tops sparingly with melted ghee. Aim for an even 3–4 mm thickness; repair cracks before the piece reaches the hot surface.

Bake until the lower surfaces brown, turn each patty, and continue until the edges feel firm. Keep the oven at 200°C (400°F) for 20–24 minutes, checking until a thin knife slides through the largest piece without resistance.
Set Vrat Baked Yam Patties on a rack or heatproof board for 6 minutes so steam escapes without softening the browned surfaces; serve while the center is still warm.
items.guidance: Chestnut meal gives these festival yam patties structure without grain Vata: serve it warm and add a little ghee if the meal feels dry. Pitta: keep the sharp spices modest and favor coriander or fennel. Kapha: eat one thin patty and use little ghee.
provenance: original lacto-vegetarian recipe developed for the R3 regional and practical cooking collection

items.name: Vrat Baked Green Plantain Cutlets
steps: Finish the listed preparation for the green plantain, amaranth grain, and cumin seeds before lighting the burner, and keep each addition ready in the order it will be used.

Work the mashed plantain with crushed popped amaranth, cumin, pepper, and salt until evenly combined. Work over steady low heat for 7–9 minutes; continue when until the surface looks dry, brown freckles appear, and the center springs back.

Form small oval cutlets, place them on a greased tray, and brush their exposed sides lightly with ghee. Keep the layer loose and even, with no pooled liquid, so every portion receives the same balance.

Bake until set, turn the cutlets carefully, and finish when both surfaces are dry and golden. Keep the oven at 200°C (400°F) for 20–24 minutes, checking until the surface looks dry, brown freckles appear, and the center springs back.
Set Vrat Baked Green Plantain Cutlets on a rack or heatproof board for 5 minutes so steam escapes without softening the browned surfaces; serve while the center is still warm.
items.guidance: Popped amaranth gives baked plantain cutlets a delicate crust Vata: serve it warm and add a little ghee if the meal feels dry. Pitta: keep the sharp spices modest and favor coriander or fennel. Kapha: limit the portion and keep the ghee light.
provenance: original lacto-vegetarian recipe developed for the R3 regional and practical cooking collection

items.name: Vrat Warm Papaya Pomegranate Plate

ingredients.name: Papaya, peeled and cut into thick slices

steps: Set the papaya, pomegranate arils, and fennel seeds in separate bowls and complete the listed rinsing, cutting, or grinding before heating the pan.
Warm the papaya slices briefly in a covered pan until their chill is gone but their shape remains firm. Aim for an even 3–4 mm thickness; repair cracks before the piece reaches the hot surface.
Arrange the softened fruit on plates and scatter the pomegranate arils over the surface. Keep the layer loose and even, with no pooled liquid, so every portion receives the same balance.

Finish with crushed fennel, sliced mint, and a light squeeze of lime immediately before serving. Leave the pan off the flame for 4 minutes, then taste and correct the final balance before serving at the stated temperature.
Rest Vrat Warm Papaya Pomegranate Plate 4 minutes covered off the burner; check the final consistency and serve it warm without prolonged holding.
items.guidance: Serving fruit without dairy keeps this fasting plate simple and traditionally compatible Vata: warm the papaya thoroughly and use little lime. Pitta: omit the lime if the fruit is already tart. Kapha: keep the portion moderate.

items.name: Vrat Almond Date Laddoo
steps: Complete the chopping and grinding for the dates, almonds, and dried coconut, then set each component beside the stove in the order it enters the recipe.

Warm the chopped dates in a dry pan until they soften into a sticky mass. Give the spices about 30 seconds before adding the larger pieces, then continue over low heat for 4–5 minutes, moving the pan often, until the raw aroma is gone.

Fold in the coarse almonds, shredded coconut, cardamom, and warmed coconut oil until evenly distributed. Mix for 2 minutes with the heat off, stopping when the seasonings are even and a pressed spoonful holds together without crumbling.
Cool the mixture just enough to handle, then roll small festival balls and let them firm uncovered. Aim for an even 2–3 mm thickness; repair cracks before the piece reaches the hot surface.
Rest Vrat Almond Date Laddoo 3 minutes covered off the burner; check the final consistency and serve it warm without prolonged holding.
items.guidance: Dates bind these dairy-free fasting sweets without added sugar Vata: serve it warm and add a little ghee if the meal feels dry. Pitta: keep the sharp spices modest and favor coriander or fennel. Kapha: eat only one small ball.

items.name: Vrat Taro Lotus Seed Pot

ingredients.name: Taro root, peeled and cut into chunks
Fresh ginger, cut into fine slivers

steps: Set aside 580 ml (about 2 1/2 cups) freshly boiled water for Vrat Taro Lotus Seed Pot, reserving about 60 ml to correct the final consistency.
Parboil the taro chunks until their surfaces soften, drain them carefully, and leave them intact. Let it drain for 1 minute without pressing harder than the recipe's texture requires.

Toast cumin and ginger slivers in ghee, add the taro, and turn the pieces until their edges take on color. Give the spices about 30 seconds before adding the larger pieces, then continue over medium-low heat for 3–4 minutes, moving the pan often, until the raw aroma is gone.

Pour in hot water and the roasted lotus-seed halves, simmer until the broth thickens, and season the fasting pot. Maintain gentle medium heat for 13–15 minutes, stirring every 5 minutes, until a thin knife slides through the largest piece without resistance.
Rest Vrat Taro Lotus Seed Pot 4 minutes covered off the burner; check the final consistency and serve it warm without prolonged holding.
items.guidance: Ginger and crisp lotus seeds balance the grounding weight of taro Vata: serve it warm and add a little ghee if the meal feels dry. Pitta: keep the sharp spices modest and favor coriander or fennel. Kapha: choose a small portion and use less ghee.
